name: Fire Fighting / Fixed Firewater System
zones: fire suppression for electrical & process risk rooms

activities: pump house slab / plinths and equipment foundations
firewater tank foundation or reservoir civil works
underground mains trenching, thrust blocks and bedding
sleeves, penetrations and fire-rated openings through structure
riser shaft readiness and floor penetrations
sequence.note: Civil enters only as enabler: foundations, buried-main trenches, sleeves and shaft openings must be ready before firewater equipment/pipe sets.

activities: set fire pumps (electric duty, diesel standby, jockey) on plinths
install firewater tank / connect suction
erect riser standpipes and sectional isolation valves
lay and joint underground ring main / hydrant loop
erect above-ground distribution, risers and branch mains
install sprinkler/deluge heads, spray nozzles and hydrants/monitors
install hangers, supports, seismic bracing and flushing connections
power to pump controllers and jockey pump
wire pump status, running and low-pressure signals to fire alarm/BMS
flow switch, tamper switch and pressure switch terminations
deluge/preaction release solenoid and detection interconnection
flush underground mains and distribution to remove debris
verify no blockage at heads/hydrants before pressurisation
sequence.note: Flushing before hydrostatic test is mandatory; skipping it causes blocked heads and failed acceptance.

activities: hydrostatic pressure test of underground mains (extended hold)
hydrostatic test of above-ground piping and risers
witnessed pressure hold and leak/joint acceptance
walk-down of head coverage, spacing and obstruction
punch list clearance for the system
pump no-load / churn test, alignment and rotation check
diesel engine dry run, fuel and battery checks
controller sequence and set-point configuration
full-flow pump performance test against curve (churn/rated/peak)
auto-start on pressure drop, jockey/duty/standby cascade test
deluge/preaction functional release with detection
hydrant/monitor flow and pressure verification
cause-and-effect with fire alarm and integrated shutdown

typical_relationships.reason: Buried pipe cannot be laid until the trench is excavated, bedded and thrust blocks are cast.
Pumps are grouted to their plinths; the foundation must exist and cure first.
You can only flush a piping run once it is fully erected and connected end to end.
Flushing must remove construction debris before pressurisation, or heads and valves foul and the test fails.

typical_relationships.after: Fire pump full-flow performance / functional commissioning
typical_relationships.reason: The distribution must prove leak-tight and pressure-holding before pumps run at rated flow into it.
All terminal devices must be fitted so the whole system is tested at once as installed.
Controllers must be powered and signal-terminated before automatic start logic can be proven.

typical_relationships.after: Cause-and-effect / integrated fire test with fire alarm
typical_relationships.reason: Integrated cause-and-effect assumes the firewater supply is already proven to deliver rated flow and pressure.
Vertical piping routes through pre-formed penetrations; forming them after erection means re-work.

interfaces.requirement: Permanent (or commissioning) power to the electric fire-pump controller and jockey pump before any pump run test.
Fire alarm / detection panel live and addressed before deluge/preaction release and cause-and-effect testing.
Pump-house foundations, buried-main trenches, thrust blocks and structural penetrations complete before setting equipment and laying mains.
Firewater tank filled from a raw/utility water source before flushing and hydrostatic test.
Pump running/fault and low-pressure status signals published to BMS/fire graphics.
Pipe-rack / support steel and seismic bracing in place before above-ground distribution is hung.

testing_requirements: Flushing of underground mains and distribution before pressure test
Hydrostatic pressure test of underground mains at elevated pressure with extended hold
Hydrostatic pressure test of above-ground piping and risers with witnessed hold
Fire pump performance test across churn, rated and 150% (peak) flow points against the pump curve
Automatic start on pressure drop and duty/standby/jockey cascade sequence test
Deluge/preaction functional release verification with detection
Diesel-driven pump run, fuel autonomy and battery/start reliability check
commissioning_dependencies: Permanent or temporary commissioning power to pump controllers
Fire alarm & detection panel live for release and cause-and-effect
Firewater tank filled from a water source
Piping mechanically complete, flushed and hydro-tested
System punch list cleared to a level that permits energisation
Instrument/pressure switch and flow-switch loops calibrated
typical_exceptions: Small dry-pipe or pre-action zones may hydro-test with air/nitrogen rather than water
Gaseous/clean-agent suppression rooms follow their own cylinder discharge test path, not water hydrostatic
Where a public/utility firewater supply exists, an on-site pump set and tank may be reduced or omitted
Foam systems add a concentrate proportioning test not present on plain water systems
evidence: Fire-pump performance and cause-and-effect commissioning are scheduled before the firewater mains are flushed and hydrostatically tested, or before pump power / fire-alarm detection is live — a physically impossible order for firewater acceptance.
